# stickfin / "Anti Broke" channel — reference for AI tools

This file exists so any AI assistant picking up this repo — a fresh Claude
session, another tool, whatever — has the context that took a full night of
real trial-and-error to establish, without re-deriving it from scratch or
repeating fixes already made (or mistakes already caught) once.

## Starting a new chat? Paste this to the new AI first

> I'm continuing work on "Anti Broke" (stickfin), an autonomous personal-finance
> Shorts channel. Read `llms.txt` at the repo root first, in full — it has the
> architecture (also see README.md/SETUP.md), everything fixed in the last
> session, and — most important — the conclusion that session reached about
> whether the current AI-generated-character-art approach is actually viable.
> Read the "Is this approach viable?" section especially carefully before
> assuming we just keep patching the same pipeline. Once you've read it, tell
> me what you understand the current state to be, then I'll tell you what I
> want to do today.

## Is this approach viable? Read this before doing anything else

Short answer: the user ended the last session concluding **no, not as-is** —
"looks like this approach will not work." That session was one long chain of
finding a real, visible, ship-quality defect, fixing it, and finding the next
one, across every asset category the pipeline touches:

- Character poses: missing mouths, a bald crown on the long-hair character
  (3 of 14 poses in one video, 0 in another — inconsistent, not deterministic),
  duplicate "twin" figures from a reference-sheet bug, a branded logo patch
  that read backwards when mirrored, rembg (background removal) punching
  random holes in torsos/necks that let the scene bleed through.
- Layout: a prop template that placed a prop overlapping BOTH characters in a
  2-person shot; the first fix attempt made it WORSE (66% overlap -> 84%)
  because the real gap between two characters varies by pose and can be
  narrower than assumed.
- The shared icon library (32 icons, reused across every video): 9 of 32 were
  found fully or partially hollow (transparent interior) on first inspection.
  After fixing the prompt and regenerating, **the same specific icons kept
  coming back broken on subsequent regenerations** — `shield`, `comment`,
  `bookmark`, `handshake` failed hollow-fill compliance 2-3 rounds in a row
  regardless of how explicit the "fill completely, never hollow" instruction
  was made. A manually-applied deterministic fix (flood-fill the enclosed
  interior with the correct colour, found via alpha-mask topology) was needed
  in the end — twice, because the first attempt at that manual fix ALSO had a
  bug (a hole leaking through a 1-2px gap in the outline stroke swallowed a
  much larger area than intended on `shield`).
- Captions: skit-format videos were shipping with ZERO on-screen text for the
  entire back-and-forth dialogue (just one static hook line for the whole
  video) — a genuine functional gap, not a polish issue, live on real
  published videos before it was caught.

**The pattern, not just the individual bugs**: every fix category needed
2-3 iterations before it actually held, and fixing one asset class did not
predict whether another asset class had the same problem — each one had to be
independently, exhaustively checked at full resolution (thumbnail-scale
review reliably missed real defects — e.g. the bald-crown gap was invisible
at 400px review height, obvious at real viewing size). That's a lot of manual
QA surface for a channel that's supposed to run unattended.

**What's actually fixed as of this file being written**: everything found
IS fixed and verified (see changelog below) — the pipeline as it stands
tonight should not reproduce any of the specific bugs listed above. The open
question the user wants addressed in a fresh chat is whether to keep
hardening this same AI-generation approach indefinitely (each new topic/pose
combination is a chance for a NEW instance of "AI didn't comply with an
explicit instruction"), or switch to something structurally less exposed to
this failure mode — e.g. a fixed library of pre-made/hand-designed character
art reused across all videos instead of generating new pose art per video,
a proper commercial character-animation tool/asset pack, or something else.
**Don't assume the answer — that's the discussion to have.** But do bring
this history so the discussion starts from real evidence, not guessing.

## What this project does (see README.md and SETUP.md for full detail)

Daily GitHub Actions cron: picks a personal-finance topic (`themes.yaml`),
writes a script (Gemini/Vertex), synthesizes TTS per beat, generates
character/prop/chart art (Nano Banana / Vertex) + cuts it out (rembg),
composites static shots with hard cuts (no Ken Burns/tweening), muxes audio +
captions, publishes to YouTube/Instagram/TikTok via Buffer.

Two formats: `short` (9:16, the daily output) and `wide` (16:9 long-form,
separate/less-used path). Two script shapes: `explainer` (one host, talks to
camera) and `skit` (host + a second character, back-and-forth dialogue).

Publishing paths (`.github/workflows/`):
- `daily.yml` — manual-dispatch, full generate-through-publish, one video.
- `batch-build.yml` + `poster.yml` — the actual automatic cadence: batch-build
  N videos ahead into `state/queue.json`, poster.yml drains one per scheduled
  firing (4x/day), no Vertex call needed on the posting side.
- `publish-now.yml` — publish an already-committed `media/<slug>.mp4`
  immediately, bypassing the queue. Used for the hand-authored one-offs this
  session (see below).

## Session changelog (most recent first — this is what actually got fixed)

All committed to `main`, no open uncommitted work.

- `2e5f5b7`, `62b0700` — **icon library overhaul.** Moved the white
  sticker-border from an AI prompt instruction (unreliable: clean on solid
  shapes, ragged on thin-line icons like chart-up/down, inconsistent even on
  some round ones) to a deterministic code step (dilate the alpha mask by a
  fixed radius, fill the ring white — `tools/build_icons.py:_add_border`).
  Fixed hollow fills on 13 of 32 icons total across multiple rounds: bookmark,
  comment, handshake, house, shield, bars-down, receipt, question, scale,
  coin, lightbulb, warning, piggy-bank (some self-corrected on regeneration,
  many needed the manual flood-fill in the end). `tools/build_icons.py` is
  the one-time-generation tool (`python tools/build_icons.py --force
  <name>...`) — icons are committed, never regenerated automatically.
- `5f61bac` — removed 6 stale queue entries from `state/queue.json` that
  were queued 2026-09-01 (weeks before every fix this session) and would
  have kept auto-posting old-broken-design videos on the regular 4x/day
  poster schedule regardless of any code fix.
- `4ad66d8` — `assets._cutout()`: patch SMALL rembg segmentation holes only
  (below ~0.6% of the figure's own opaque area, per connected component).
  A blanket "fill every hole" first attempt was wrong — it would have
  destroyed legitimate anatomical negative space (the gap under an akimbo
  arm, inside a circular hand gesture) by filling it with garbage-coloured
  blobs. Calibrated against confirmed real defects (~1000-1100px) vs
  confirmed legitimate gaps (6,000-35,000px+).
- `fa1ea62` — fixed the long-hair second character's hair prompt to
  explicitly require full crown coverage (was: "long flowing hair framing
  both sides", which let the model draw a side-swept style with a bald gap
  on top — invisible at thumbnail review, obvious at real size, confirmed
  via a live published video's actual Instagram screenshot).
- `503bef5` — `captions.py`: skit-format videos ("title" caption style) were
  showing ONE static hook line for the WHOLE video and never captioning the
  actual dialogue. Fixed: the hook now covers only beat 1, every beat after
  gets a word-by-word reveal caption highlighted in brand green
  (`config.CAP_SPOKEN`), same mechanism explainer format already used.
  `layout.py`: fixed a 2-character-plus-prop template that placed the prop
  overlapping both characters (first fix attempt made it worse, 66% -> 84%
  overlap, because the actual per-pose gap between characters isn't the
  nominal template gap — moved the prop to the open band above both
  characters' heads instead, where it structurally can't collide).
- `a995e4d`, `fd4b27e` — rewrote the script-writing prompt (`generate.py`
  SYSTEM/SCHEMA_DOC) twice, per direct user feedback: (1) dropped the fixed
  "6-8 beats, 20-28s" target so stories run as long as they need (soft
  ceiling: ~90s, the real Instagram Reels classification limit) and required
  causal connectors between beats instead of standalone punchy fragments;
  (2) fixed a "short sentences" rule that was producing staccato ad-copy
  cadence ("No. On the entire amount. From day one.") — now explicitly
  requires natural spoken rhythm with contractions and normal connectors.
- `0f46b6b`, `3da0f5c`, `b064a96` — character/compositor fixes: reference
  sheet was drawing TWO views of the same character (front + 3/4), which
  biased pose generation toward drawing two people instead of one (confirmed
  live: 3 of ~8 poses in a published video shipped with a visible duplicate
  "twin"). Fixed to draw one view. Added a proper branded female second
  character (paired with the existing "Aoede" TTS voice) instead of an
  unbranded generic one. Fixed the compositor's facing/mirror logic, which
  only considered charts/props when deciding which way a character faces —
  a plain two-person dialogue shot left both characters facing the same
  direction instead of each other. Replaced the host's "ANTI BROKE" text
  wordmark patch with a single "A" monogram (vertically symmetric) after
  finding the wordmark read backwards whenever the mirror logic flipped a
  character — first attempt at just saying "draw only a letter" wasn't
  enough, the model kept echoing the brand name from elsewhere in the same
  prompt; removing the literal brand name from the prompt text fixed it.
- `d95999c` and earlier — the original character redesign: replaced the old
  bare-line stick figure with a fully-illustrated flat-vector character
  (the "sharp" look the user asked for after seeing a competitor reel),
  kept the faceless flat round head (brand identity), gave the host a
  charcoal bomber jacket + branded patch. This is the redesign that then
  needed all the follow-up fixes above.
- `028dec1` — forced every scene to a flat background colour for ALL
  formats (was: explainer-only; skit could still get an AI-drawn scene,
  which is what triggered the character-quality conversation that led to
  the redesign above).

Two hand-authored one-off videos were built and published this session as
originals (NOT reproductions) after the user brought real competitor scripts
as "make something like this" requests that turned out to be near-verbatim
copies of other creators' actual published videos (one ending in another
account's Instagram handle, one in another's watermark). Declined to
reproduce those directly; wrote original scripts on the same underlying
mechanism instead, and declined outright a third request (a Twitch donation-
manipulation "money idea" script — that one isn't a grey-area tax trick, it's
a scheme to defraud a streamer's own audience, not something to produce
regardless of format):
- `billionaire-watch-tax-trick` — freeport / buy-borrow-die mechanism,
  corrected a claim the source material got backwards (collectibles are
  taxed WORSE than stocks, ~28% vs ~20%; the real advantage is deferral +
  borrowing, not a lower rate).
- `private-jet-tax-writeoff` — US Section 179 / bonus depreciation on a
  business aircraft (the US equivalent of an India-specific source video),
  corrected the "basically a free jet" framing the same way.

Established policy, confirmed explicitly by the user each time it came up:
**already-published videos are left as-is when a bug is found after the
fact** (background-colour bug, duplicate-figure bug, bald-crown bug all
shipped on real posts before being caught) — fixes apply going forward only,
no takedown/repost, unless the user says otherwise for a specific case.

## Things discussed but NOT implemented

- **Fixed-zone layout idea** (user's proposal): define fixed screen regions
  per role (e.g. lower-left = male character, lower-right = female, upper =
  props/charts, all on the same flat background so it reads as one frame),
  instead of the current dynamic per-shot layout solver. Assessed as a good
  idea for the skit (2-character) case specifically — would eliminate the
  layout-collision bug CLASS by construction rather than by collision-
  avoidance math that can fail on some future pose combination. Would NOT
  have prevented the rembg-hole or hollow-icon defects (different problem).
  Not built — conversation moved to the broader "is this approach even
  right" question before implementation started.

## Credentials / access

See `SETUP.md` for the full list. Quick pointers: GCP project id and Vertex
setup mirror `core-decor-automation` (see that repo's `llms.txt` for the
working WIF/service-account pattern if auth needs re-deriving). Buffer
API key + channel IDs are GitHub Actions secrets only, NOT available in a
local shell — `tools/publish_now.py` / the `Publish Now` workflow is the
way to post a specific already-committed video without them locally.
